display.title: Episode 303: The Golden Staff, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: The brachah Pokeach Ivrim and all the mitzvos we do with our eyes, then the start of 'The Golden Staff': a poor woodchopper's wish that everything he touches turn to gold.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in Kislev 5748. Continuing the series on starting the day right, Uncle Yossi explains the morning brachah Pokeach Ivrim: just as a bulb needs electricity, our eyes need Hashem's power to see. He lists the mitzvos we do with our eyes, from the Havdalah flame, the Chanukah lights and seeing the Torah at Hagbah to Kiddush Levanah, tzitzis, the blossoming trees of Nissan, lightning, the rainbow and the face of a tzaddik, and asks children to look only at good and modest things, until our eyes see the coming of Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march, story time begins 'The Golden Staff'. Binyamin, a poor woodchopper in Poland, cries out to Hashem that he works so hard for a few copper coins. A radiant old stranger appears and grants him two wishes, and Binyamin wishes that everything he touches turn to gold. Between the two halves, a ten-year-old yeshiva boy leads the Shema. Binyamin's bundle of sticks turns to gold, but riches bring him greater tests, and he grows greedy. To be continued. The show ends with Shabbos candle time and news of gifts for new candle lighters and Tzivos Hashem rooms.
display.lesson: Thank Hashem for the gift of sight and use your eyes only for good things; riches can be a harder test than poverty.
